title: LOOKUP chooses search axis by cols > rows in 2-arg form, requires a 1-row/1-col result_vector in 3-arg form, and returns #VALUE! on blank vectors
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, LOOKUP(lookup_value, lookup_vector, [result_vector]) bisects in two-argument form along the first row (returning from the last row) when columns > rows and along the first column (last column) otherwise. In three-argument form it returns #N/A if result_vector has both >1 rows and >1 columns, if either vector is a multi-area reference, or if a result_vector array is shorter than the matched index; returns #VALUE! if lookup_vector or result_vector is omitted or blank (LOOKUP(1,) or LOOKUP(1,A1:A6,)); and ignores unsorted errors during bisection (LOOKUP(2,{1,#DIV/0!,1,#DIV/0!}) -> 1). All 3,360 full-bank LOOKUP rows match.
basis: Measured in DnaCalc cfunc_m3_6 (lookup_edges rows 117-128, 173-175, 303-307, 458-466, Excel 16.0.20527.20088); 3,360/3,360 full-bank rows match.
